target_customer: Individuals (mostly young builders and creators) joining cohort programs to build personal projects; sponsors and partners supported the programs
problem: People want to start personal projects but lack community, accountability and structure.
business_model: Free online cohort programs (nights and weekends, six weeks) funded by venture capital, with sponsorships and later a paid in-person school
product_category: Online education and community for builders

founders.name: Farza Majeed
previous_startups: ZipSchool, an online elementary school with over 100K students
founders.background_notes: Based on founder letters and a DEV Community profile; the YC page lists no founder bios.

exit.reason: Founder stepped back citing his mental health and loss of drive, per a newsletter summary of his letter

technical_complexity.rationale: Web platform and cohort tooling; the hard parts were community building and content, not engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Community of tens of thousands of participants gave some pull, but programs and content could be copied by other cohort communities and depended on one founder's energy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent targeted it; the company ended by founder choice in 2024.

market_need_then: Pandemic era remote learning and a surge of people starting side projects; over 30K joined nights and weekends and over 3K shipped projects per its own account.

identity.voice_and_tone: Warm, personal, informal and nostalgic; always lowercase, ends with love you

branding.brand_signature: Nights and weekends program and the Hogwarts for builders and dreamers framing
branding.community_and_virality: Large online community of builders with founder newsletters and a farewell page; cited as having trained 125,000 builders by one source.

brand_strength.rationale: A distinctive founder voice and lowercase identity drove strong community loyalty and organic sharing among young builders, though evidence is from founder posts and newsletters.

pivots.why: The team shifted away from ZipSchool toward buildspace per a founder Substack post.

outcome_analysis: buildspace grew a large free community through its nights and weekends cohorts, raised 10M USD led by a16z in November 2022 and trained a claimed 125,000 builders. It closed in 2024 with a farewell page and the founder's letter; a newsletter summary attributes the end to his mental health and loss of drive, not to a lack of demand or money. Single founder dependence was the key risk, coded as other. A later revival on Product Hunt in January 2025 is noted.
notes: Round type conflicts: seed (CB Insights, dated 2022-11-18), seed announced March 2022 (VCBacked), Series A at 100M USD valuation (everydev.ai, unverified). The 10M USD amount and a16z lead are stated in the founder's own post. Shutdown date of August 2024 comes from one aggregator; the closure reason comes from a secondary newsletter, not the primary letter. A revival listing on Product Hunt dated January 2025 suggests programs resumed, conflicting with the YC Inactive status. No dated competitor sources were found for mid 2020, so the competitor list is empty.
